title: Your first C++ program: from source to a verifiable report
goal: Read every line of a first program and identify its actual result.

prerequisites.text: You can open the editor and perform the small calculation from the first topic.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: A program is a text of instructions. The environment builds it, then runs it. Editor text, standard input stdin, output stdout and build messages are different things. This example has empty input because it reads nothing.

#include <iostream> provides output facilities. int main() { begins the main function; braces enclose its statements. std::cout is standard output; << sends text or a number to it here. The string literal "Hello" is text in double quotes. '\n' is a newline character. ; ends a statement.

return 0 passes a successful exit status to the environment; it does not write 0 to output. The environment prepares execution before main. Read << as output here; its other uses belong to later material.

sections.title: Read every line of a first program and identify its actual result.
trace: Declarations are available; this is not an output statement.
The statements in the body begin to execute.
Quotes are not printed; the newline separates the next line.
First the expression produces 5, then output displays it.
Zero is an exit status, not a third output line.

sections.title: Change one condition and check the prediction
paragraphs: Replace Hello with Welcome and 2 + 3 with 7 + 4.
Edit the text inside the double quotes.
Keep the two output statements and both newlines.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: A missing ; usually prevents a build. Replacing + with - may build but produces a different result. After a failed build, old stdout is not the output of the new source.

sections.title: Now solve your own task
paragraphs: Write two output lines: Ready and the result of 6 × 7. Explain why there is no third line containing 0.
Practice contains a separate starter. Predict the result before changing your program. Returning to the example does not replace your source.

selfcheck.prompt: What output follows the specified change? Replace Hello with Welcome and 2 + 3 with 7 + 4.
selfcheck.feedback: Edit the text inside the double quotes. Keep the two output statements and both newlines.

selfcheck.prompt: Write two output lines: Ready and the result of 6 × 7. Explain why there is no third line containing 0.
selfcheck.feedback: Compare the output with the readable reference case below. Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic. There must be two lines: Ready and 42. Replacing 6*7 with 6+7 gives 13 on the second line. return 0 does not add a line containing 0; an old stdout after a build error does not prove a new run.

practice.title: Independent variation
practice.task: Write two output lines: Ready and the result of 6 × 7. Explain why there is no third line containing 0.
criteria: Compare the output with the readable reference case below.
Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic.
There must be two lines: Ready and 42. Replacing 6*7 with 6+7 gives 13 on the second line. return 0 does not add a line containing 0; an old stdout after a build error does not prove a new run.

steps.action: Write two output lines: Ready and the result of 6 × 7. Explain why there is no third line containing 0.
Write your solution in a separate starter; keep your previous work.
Compare actual output with your prediction and explain any difference.

terms.definition: Program text checked and translated by a compiler before execution.
The special function that begins the user-written part of a normal hosted C++ program after runtime setup.
The standard output stream; Code Studio displays its content in the result area.
In int boxes = 3;, a named integer object is created with the initial value 3.
A status value returned when the program ends; 0 indicates success and is not a printed character.
